content.title: Who was Nick Jonas 'sister' he lost? Remembering Maya Kibbel
content.text: Nick Jonas, known worldwide for his music and acting career, faced a deeply personal loss with the passing of his sister figure, Maya Kibbel. Kibbel, who grew up alongside the Jonas brothers and was considered their “sister,” passed away at 30 after battling Wilson’s disease, a rare genetic disorder that causes copper to accumulate in the body. Her death has been widely reported, but what makes her memory especially poignant is the way Nick himself chose to honor her on her birthday. The Gut Punch hitmaker took to Instagram Stories to share a childhood photo of the two of them together. Priyanka Chopra’s husband accompanied the throwback photo with a heartfelt message, “I reached for my phone to call you so many times today, because for as long as I can remember this has been your day. Your birthday — April 3rd, seared in my memory. I will cherish the time God gave us together forever. Please be at peace in heaven now, and blow out your candles with the angels. You are and always will be my sister. I miss you so much. Happy birthday Maya.” The post reflected the depth of their connection. Though Kibbel was not a biological sibling, she was part of the Jonas household from an early age. Her presence was woven into their family story, and Nick’s tribute made clear that her role in his life was as significant as any blood relative. She battled Wilson’s disease, a rare genetic disorder that causes copper to accumulate in the body, leading to life threatening complications if untreated. Reports note that she had been struggling with the illness, which can affect the liver, brain, and other vital organs. Her passing has drawn attention to the early warning signs of Wilson’s disease, including fatigue, jaundice, tremors, and difficulty with speech or coordination. In her final social media posts, Kibbel reflected on her friendships and childhood memories, leaving behind words that resonated with fans and those who knew her personally. For Nick, who has often spoken about the importance of family, losing someone who grew up as part of his inner circle marks a painful chapter.
